diagnostics.message: :resource.helm_release.karpenter: explicit depends_on of :module.karpenter is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class: explicit depends_on of :module.eks is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class: explicit depends_on of :module.karpenter is redundant — already implied by attribute references
:resource.null_resource.update_kubeconfig: explicit depends_on of :module.eks is redundant — already implied by attribute references

`null_resource.delete_daemonset` removes the aws-node (AWS VPC CNI) daemonset from kube-system, but it only depends on `null_resource.update_kubeconfig` and `module.eks` — nothing ties it to `null_resource.create_calico_installation`. With Calico as the CNI, removing aws-node before Calico is actually installed/available leaves pods without working networking (and new nodes unable to register). The delete must be ordered after the Calico Installation is created; no attribute reference or depends_on currently expresses that.

`null_resource.update_kubeconfig` explicitly depends_on `module.eks`, but its own triggers/local-exec already reference `module.eks.cluster_name`, which is already recorded as an implicit dependency — the explicit depends_on adds nothing.

`data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster` explicitly depends_on `module.eks`, but it also depends_on `time_sleep.wait_300_seconds`, which itself depends_on `module.eks`. Ordering after the sleep already guarantees the cluster exists; the extra `module.eks` entry is redundant.

`data.aws_eks_cluster_auth.cluster` explicitly depends_on `module.eks`, but `time_sleep.wait_300_seconds` (already in its depends_on) depends on `module.eks`, so the cluster ordering is already established transitively.

`data.aws_ecrpublic_authorization_token.token` explicitly depends_on `module.eks`, but it already depends_on `time_sleep.wait_300_seconds`, which depends_on `module.eks` — the ordering is already implied.

`helm_release.karpenter` explicitly depends_on `module.karpenter`, but its `values` heredoc already references `module.karpenter.service_account` and `module.karpenter.queue_name`, so `module.karpenter` is already an implicit dependency.

`null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class` explicitly depends_on `module.eks`, but its triggers and local-exec manifest already reference `module.eks.cluster_primary_security_group_id` / `module.eks.cluster_security_group_id`, so the dependency is already implicit.

`null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class` explicitly depends_on `module.karpenter` (via `module.karpenter.node_iam_role_arn`), but `triggers`/the manifest already reference `module.karpenter.node_iam_role_arn`, making it an implicit dependency already.

`null_resource.delete_daemonset` explicitly depends_on `module.eks`, but `null_resource.update_kubeconfig` (also in its depends_on) itself depends on `module.eks`, so the cluster ordering is already transitive.

`null_resource.apply_node_pool` explicitly depends_on `module.eks`, but it already depends_on `null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class`, which depends on `module.eks` (and references it directly) — the cluster ordering is already established transitively.

`null_resource.apply_node_pool` explicitly depends_on `helm_release.karpenter`, but it already depends_on `null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class`, which depends on `helm_release.karpenter`, so the Karpenter-install ordering is already transitive.

`null_resource.apply_node_pool` explicitly depends_on `null_resource.update_kubeconfig`, but `null_resource.apply_ec2_node_class` (already in its depends_on) depends on `null_resource.update_kubeconfig`, so kubeconfig setup is already ordered ahead transitively.
